title: Anonymous in Name Only: A Critical Review and a Reidentification Exercise on the European Commission's Anonymization Measures for Google Search Data under Article 6(11) of the DMA
abstract: arXiv:2611.17012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In July 2026, the European Commission (EC) set out the anonymization measures Alphabet must implement to share Google Search data with competing search engines under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act. As the first concrete illustration of how the EC operationalizes anonymization under the EU digital rulebook, this methodology could become a regulatory benchmark. In this paper, we show why it should not. We critically review the anonymization measures proposed by the EC, from the characterization of residual risk to the suppression thresholds and the reliance on contractual safeguards. For each of those issues, we highlight significant conceptual flaws, and, where applicable, we illustrate these flaws with empirical observations from real Google Search data provided by Alphabet and protected under the EC's measures. Importantly, we present examples of low-effort reidentification, record linkage, and confidential attribute

translated_title: 仅名义上的匿名化：对欧盟委员会依据《数字市场法》第6(11)条针对谷歌搜索数据所制定匿名化措施的批判性审查与重识别实验
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.17012v2 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：2026年7月，欧盟委员会（EC）规定了Alphabet必须实施的匿名化措施，以便依据《数字市场法》（DMA）第6(11)条与竞争对手搜索引擎共享谷歌搜索数据。作为欧盟数字规则框架下委员会如何具体落实匿名化的首个实例，该方法论可能成为监管基准。本文论证了其不应成为基准的原因。我们对欧盟委员会提出的匿名化措施进行了批判性审查，涵盖残余风险的界定、抑制阈值以及对合同保障措施的依赖等方面。针对每一个问题，我们都指出了重大的概念性缺陷，并在适用情况下，利用Alphabet提供的、受欧盟委员会措施保护的真实谷歌搜索数据的实证观察来展示这些缺陷。重要的是，我们给出了低工作量重识别、记录链接以及机密属性
tldr: 本文批判性地审查了欧盟委员会依据《数字市场法》第6(11)条为谷歌搜索数据共享所制定的匿名化措施，指出其存在重大概念缺陷，并通过在真实数据上的低成本重识别实验证明该方法不应成为监管基准。
